scope: Eight selected same-checkpoint fixed16 cases, normal/noC/direct-only/Q-off, frames0/20/40/60/80. Sentinel selection is not an all60 pass rate.

cases.VP002: Normal and direct-only produce extra crossed slats; noC late splits. Q-off retains a thin single strip but becomes pale and does not convincingly bend into a bow.
cases.VP004: Normal retains ruler with fracture but little visible bending. Direct-only replaces it with a thick ridged beam with melted fracture; noC keeps a bar and fractures. Q-off preserves recognizable ruler shape best, but process still incomplete.
cases.VP009: Direct-only/noC restore brighter worker/glass/picture identity compared with normal. Suction tool and actual glass lifting remain incomplete. Q-off similarly preserves geometry but is pale/static.
cases.VP015: All modes fail the complete rower/oar interaction. Normal distorts long boat/oar structures; noC/direct-only show floating boat-like structures. Q-off makes a bent oar without a convincing rower.
cases.VP016: Normal dark blurred leaf omits probe, direct-only restores a visible probe/insect, noC shows clear probe and leaf. This is a concrete visual and semantic improvement after removing associated writing.
cases.VP026: Normal is very dark and replaces requested cord/people with broad red fabric; direct-only/noC restore people but still broad fabric and shape errors. Q-off restores a rope-like span, not a clean complete interaction.
cases.VP034: Normal/direct-only/noC fill much of the image with balloon surfaces; Q-off retains a whole balloon with little convincing inflation. Visibility improves but does not prove the process.
cases.VP038: Normal retains roller at start then crops it out. NoC retains roller longer; direct-only and Q-off have disappearing/bending handle/roller. No mode establishes a complete accepted coating process.

conclusions: T2V associated write and learned-Q enhancement reduce SA in this checkpoint; both have zero SA wins versus their respective removal across fixed16.
Direct-only improves some real content (notably016/009) but does not fix002/004/015/026/038; a deletion alone is insufficient.
